title: Anchored ±8 nm Refinement with [70,130] nm Thickness Window and History-Seeded Population
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness mutation amplitude to ±8 nm while anchoring 40% of the optimization population to the iteration-25 best candidate (score 0.9827530417757153) will prevent the large destructive parameter jumps that caused score regressions in rounds 3, 4, and 8, while the [70,130] nm thickness window improves manufacturability without sacrificing the dual-band spectral performance.
design_principle: Local refinement around a verified high-performing design with bounded mutation amplitude prevents optimization from escaping the basin of attraction of the global optimum, while thickness window constraints ensure fabrication feasibility.
proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating TiO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, starting with TiO2 at the incident medium interface and ending with SiO2 at the substrate interface
design_variables: optimization step size bounded to ±8 nm per iteration
40% population seeded from iteration-25 best candidate
soft_objectives: Minimize crosstalk (transmittance in 450-650 nm, reflectance in 700-1000 nm)
Maintain all layer thicknesses within [70, 130] nm window
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness window [70, 130] nm ensures deposition controllability
Alternating high/low index sequence compatible with standard ion-assisted deposition
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack initialization provides physically motivated starting point for local optimization
Needle optimization with bounded step size prevents destructive parameter jumps
Tolerance analysis during design phase verifies robustness before fabrication
expected_advantages: Prevents score regression by limiting mutation amplitude
Anchors optimization near verified optimum (0.9828 from round 7)
Maintains 24-layer constraint while exploring local neighborhood
known_risks: Thickness window [70, 130] nm may exclude optimal thin layers from iteration-25 design (which had layers as thin as 31.7 nm)
Local optimization may converge to local optimum if initial seed is not in basin of global optimum
45° incidence introduces polarization splitting not present at normal incidence
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate at 45° incidence using TiO2 (high index) and SiO2 (low index) in alternating sequence. Layer 1 (incident side) is TiO2, layer 24 (substrate side) is SiO2. Initialize 40% of the optimization population with the exact thickness sequence from iteration 25 best candidate: [31.71, 83.18, 96.27, 118.44, 47.59, 92.97, 82.44, 107.21, 60.11, 97.03, 70.18, 111.24, 55.68, 105.93, 54.09, 83.96, 40.44, 75.39, 48.57, 96.17, 58.55, 96.31, 36.29, 151.03] nm. For remaining 60% of population, initialize with random thicknesses clipped to [70, 130] nm window. During gradient-based optimization, constrain thickness mutation amplitude to ±8 nm per iteration. Evaluate performance at 45° incidence for unpolarized light (average of s and p polarization). Score based on: high reflectance in 450-650 nm band, high transmittance in 700-1000 nm band, suppressed transmittance in 450-650 nm band, suppressed reflectance in 700-1000 nm band. Maximum layer count: 24. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and final thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm; minimized crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm; reflectance in 700-1000 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive from iteration 28 analysis: (1) constrains thickness mutation to ±8 nm to prevent destructive jumps that caused score regression in rounds 3, 4, 8, (2) anchors 40% of population to iteration-25 best candidate (score 0.9827530417757153) to maintain proximity to verified optimum, (3) applies [70, 130] nm thickness window for manufacturability while allowing historical seed to preserve proven thin-layer features
